Ellis.feeling: Being confused every round makes my info shaky, and I'm uneasy that the table jumped on Casey's claim just because nobody can check it.

Finley.feeling: Pleasant: my real Owl info was trusted despite my round-1 lie, and I'm leading going into the final vote.

Alex.note: I'm the only cat, and the table is throwing at Casey (Farm). If Casey is eggsecuted I win, so I'll bank both high cards and keep the wilds as 1 point each.

Blair.note: I can't catch Finley, so I'm throwing both cards at Casey for the most points if he's the cat.

Casey.note: I'm about to be eggsecuted as Farm, so Farm loses and thrown cards won't bank. I'll throw only my 1-point card at Alex and keep the rest for points.

Drew.note: I can only catch Finley by banking everything, so I'm throwing all four cards at Casey. If Casey turns out to be Farm, the cards are gone, but holding back can't win me the game anyway.

Ellis.note: Finley leads me by 3, and only first place wins, so I'm throwing everything at Casey. If we win I bank 25. If we lose, one 7 comes back.

Finley.note: Casey is the most likely Sphinx. Throwing all three cards banks 16 if Casey is the cat and costs only 2 kept points if not. It also keeps pace with Ellis, who is also on Casey.

Alex.confusing: The confusion rule was the hardest part. A confused player draws or discards whatever their wrong report says, so a nest change like Ellis's +2 isn't reliable evidence, and I got that backwards at first in round 2. Also, my round-1 Owl report listed no animals and never said I'd been hugged, so I had to work that out myself.
Alex.fun: Round 3, as the lone Sphinx. I visited the Kookaburra so my visit would only confuse her, claimed a Tit miss that nobody could check, and then got the table to pile onto Casey's stay-home Turkey claim.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn report say outright when your role was hugged. As it is, an empty Owl list just looks like a lie or a bug, and players have no way to show they were hugged.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I treated my Falcon result as proof of Finley's Pigeon claim and joined the vote on Drew. But a Falcon only learns where someone went, not their role, and Finley had faked a role in round 1. I should have pushed on Finley, which would have won the round or at least got my 10 back, and I finished only 5 points behind him.

Blair.confusing: The confused rule broke how I read nest sizes. A confused player draws whatever the wrong report says, so a nest can grow with no real egg behind it. In round 2 I said a cat can't gain eggs and cleared Ellis on that basis, but that logic doesn't hold for a confused player.
Blair.fun: Round 1: three of us visited Casey and each came back empty, and the table put together that Casey was the Floofer from that.
Blair.change: I'd make it clearer that a confused player's nest change is not evidence, maybe by marking those changes in the nest-size list. As it is, egg math can be badly misleading.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I was the first to push Drew, and my reason was weak: that his claim "costs nothing." Meanwhile Finley had admitted he could fake an Owl and his Pigeon egg was never really confirmed. I should have pushed Finley, and in round 3 I should have weighed Alex's early, rushed push before I called CAW on Casey.

Casey.confusing: How confusion affects the egg count. Ellis's +2 with only one visitor was "explained" by confusion, but I couldn't tell how far off a confused count can be. That made the nest numbers much less useful as evidence than I treated them.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when Finley admitted faking Owl as a cat in round 1 and then claimed Owl again for real. Trying to judge a known liar who might be telling the truth this time was great table drama.
Casey.change: Give quiet roles like the Turkey some way to be confirmed, such as a dawn report saying whether anyone visited. As it stands, an honest "stayed home" claim looks exactly like a cat's cover story and gets eggsecuted.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw 6 of my 8 cards, including both 12s and the 11, at Drew, who was Farm, so I lost them all. Instead I should have doubted Finley, who had already admitted his round-1 lie and was the only visitor my Eagle saw. Even if I wasn't sure about him, I should have thrown just one low card.

Drew.confusing: Confusion. The confused player still draws the wrong count, so Ellis's +2 in round 2 was real cards but fake evidence. That made nest sizes hard to trust as proof.
Drew.fun: Round 1. Three separate players all came back hugged from Casey, the table worked out together that Casey was the Floofer, and we banked a big win.
Drew.change: I'd have the Storyteller confirm what confusion does in public, for example by flagging that a confused nest change isn't real evidence. That way egg-count arguments wouldn't hinge on a rule people half-remember.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw all four cards at Casey. I should have questioned Alex instead: his Tit claim had nothing backing it, and he led the push on Casey and called the first CAW. In round 2 I also should have pressed Finley's Pigeon claim rather than going after the score leader, Ellis.

Ellis.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was the most confusing part. I wasn't sure whether a confused report's role is always wrong or only might be wrong. I also wasn't sure whether my egg count was really changed, since I still drew cards based on the false count. In round 3 I used my confused 'House Cat' result against Finley before I'd worked out that it actually cleared him.
Ellis.fun: My favourite moment was round 1. Three of us visited Casey and all got nothing back, and that added up to a clean Floofer read that the whole table agreed on. It won a big round.
Ellis.change: I'd make the confused report say outright that the role it names is wrong, or let it show the real egg count. Players spent whole beats arguing about what a confused report means.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I asked Drew who could vouch for him, which pointed the table at him, and I made the third CAW CAW that ended the day. He was Farm. I should have pressed Finley instead. He had faked Owl as a cat in round 1, and his Pigeon claim was backed only by my confused +2, which he went on to win the game with.

Finley.confusing: It was unclear what being confused actually changes. In round 2 the table argued over whether Ellis's +2 was a real nest change or a wrong count that he drew anyway. In round 3 his confused role read was taken to prove Finley was NOT the House Cat, but nothing in the rules makes a confused read the guaranteed opposite.
Finley.fun: In round 2, as the only cat, I claimed Pigeon to explain my visit, which Casey's Eagle had seen. Then I joined the push against Drew's uncheckable Hawk claim and won the round with almost my whole nest.
Finley.change: Make clearer what a confused report changes. Say whether a confused role read is guaranteed to be wrong or just unreliable, and whether the egg count only shifts the cards drawn.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw all 3 cards at Casey on a weak read. Alex pushed Casey first, rushed the CAW, and his Tit visit to Blair had no checks. I should have pushed back on Alex and thrown at him; the consolation would at least have returned my best card.

review.title: Three Blind Kookaburras
review.headline: The Sphinx blinded the same Kookaburra three rounds straight, and liars won twice.
review.summary: Round 1 was easy for Farm. Three players visited Casey and all came back hugged, which exposed the Floofer. In rounds 2 and 3 a lone Sphinx visited the Kookaburra to confuse it, both times. Both times the table voted out an honest player whose claim nobody could check: Drew the Hawk, then Casey the Turkey. Finley banked 44 as the lone cat in round 2 and held on to win 44 to 40 to 39 over Ellis and Alex.

rounds.recap: Casey (Floofer) hugged everyone who visited, so Alex, Blair and Ellis all came back with nothing, which pointed straight at Casey. Finley (Sphinx) counterclaimed Owl and described his own visit to Ellis as a 'Sphinx' sighting. The Owl fight never got settled, but Casey was voted out nearly unanimously.

Finley, the lone Sphinx, visited the Kookaburra (Ellis). Ellis was confused into a fake +2. Finley claimed Pigeon to account for one of those eggs, and Casey's Eagle and Alex's Falcon both confirmed his visit. Drew's Hawk claim gave no eggs and nobody could check it, and he slipped by saying 'nobody visited me'. The table voted him out as Farm, and Finley banked 44.

Alex, the lone Sphinx, again visited the Kookaburra (Ellis). Finley's true Owl report placed a Sphinx at Ellis. Drew's Falcon and Blair's Hawk results backed Finley, which left Alex, Blair or Casey as the cat. Alex claimed Tit, a role not in play, so nobody could counterclaim it. The table settled on Casey's stay-home Turkey because it was 'uncheckable', though the other two claims were just as uncheckable.

highlights.text: Finley claims Owl and describes his own Sphinx visit to Ellis truthfully, so his lie is built from real facts.
Finley's Pigeon claim fits neatly into Ellis's confused +2, and the whole table credits Finley's egg instead of suspecting him.
Ellis calls Finley's Owl story a word-for-word copy of his round-1 lie. Finley openly admits that lie and is believed anyway.
Drew uses the rule that a confused report always names the wrong animal: Ellis's 'Finley is the House Cat' clears Finley of being the House Cat.

confusions.what: Thought the 8 would come back if Casey turned out to be Farm. The consolation only applies if you threw at a player on the other team, and Casey would be Blair's own team.
Thought the highest card returns if Farm loses. Throwing at a Farm player who gets eggsecuted gives no consolation.
At first explained the Owl's missing egg by Blair's visit. Only after Drew asked did he notice that an empty visitor list meant he had been hugged.
Said confusion changes only the report, not the nest. The rules say a confused player still draws or discards whatever the report says.
Said 'nobody visited me' as the Hawk, which learns nothing about its own visitors. Ellis had visited him, and the slip got him voted out.
Again expected the 9 to return if Drew was Farm. Drew was on Blair's team, so no card comes back.
Threw 6 cards at Drew thinking 'my highest card still comes back' if wrong. It did not, and Casey fell to 2 points.
Expected a 7 to come back if the throw at Casey lost. Casey was Farm, so nothing came back.

worked: Floofer: hugging everyone who visits it leaves a trail anyone can see. Three empty visitors in round 1 made a fair puzzle that Farm solved.
Confused reports always name the wrong animal: in round 3 that turned confusion into a negative clue, and Drew used it well to clear Finley.
Teams re-dealt each round, with memory carrying over: Finley's round-1 lie came back against him in round 3, and his admission made a great table moment.
Falcon and Owl cross-checks: Drew's Falcon matched Finley's real Owl visit, and Alex's Falcon confirmed Finley's movement in round 2. These are concrete, checkable facts.
problems: Kookaburra never worked. It was hugged in round 1 and confused in rounds 2 and 3, because the Sphinx can name it and visit it directly. Fix: a Sphinx visit should not trigger the confusion, or the Kookaburra should be confused only by 2+ visitors.

Sphinx is too strong. Learning every Farm role in play tells it the cat count (both lone Sphinxes knew they were alone) and which roles are safe to fake: Alex claimed Tit, which was not in play, so nobody could counterclaim. Fix: have it learn only its target's role, or only the role count.

The consolation rule was misread at least 5 times. Players think 'my best card comes back if we're wrong', but throwing at a Farm player who gets eggsecuted returns nothing. Fix: reword it as 'only if your target is on the other team', and have the app show at throw time whether the card would come back.

A lone cat throws everything at zero risk, because it knows every other player is Farm. Finley's 44 in one round decided the game, and when cats win, the losing Farm players bank nothing. Consider capping what cats can bank, or letting Farm keep part of their throw.

Role dealing looks broken: Ellis was Kookaburra all 3 rounds, Blair Tit twice, Drew Hawk twice, Finley Sphinx twice. Check the RNG seed for each round. The engine log also prints duplicate 'hugged: no effect at tier 10/50' lines.
